method: Every indexed paper remains visible. Descriptions of later research are not real-world outcomes. Direction and relevance can be open questions. Editorial context snapshots are independent EU policy developments, not retroactively attributed to those papers.

editorial_context.title: EU renewable energy share, 2030 target
editorial_context.then: The 2018 Renewable Energy Directive originally set a binding EU renewable-energy share target of at least 32% by 2030. This was a policy target, not a prediction that 32% would be achieved.
editorial_context.now: The 2030 binding target was raised to at least 42.5% in 2023. Eurostat reported a 25.2% renewables share of EU gross final energy consumption for 2024, leaving a 17.3-percentage-point gap to the revised 2030 target.
editorial_context.direction: Progress observed; 2030 target not yet due; no claim of final realization.
editorial_context.relevance: This policy aim is still tracked; current relevance beyond the measured goal has not been separately reviewed.
editorial_context.open_question: How does the next comparable measurement change this picture?
editorial_context.status: Source-linked policy snapshot; not a prediction test

sources.finding: Directive revision raises target to at least 42.5%

editorial_context.title: EU net greenhouse gas reduction toward 2030
editorial_context.then: The EU policy objective is to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 relative to 1990, and become climate neutral by 2050. These are targets, not predictions.
editorial_context.now: The European Commission reported that provisional EU net greenhouse gas emissions in 2024 were 37.2% below 1990, within the scope of the EU climate target. The 2030 objective is not yet due.
editorial_context.direction: Observed emissions reductions; 2030 and 2050 objectives not yet verifiable as completed.

records.title: Will we reach the Sustainable Development Goals target for tuberculosis in the European Union/European Economic Area by 2030?
records.then: We assessed progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals target for tuberculosis in the European Union/European Economic Area using the latest tuberculosis (TB) surveillance and Eurostat data. Both the TB notification rate and the number of TB deaths were decreasing before 2015 and the TB notification rate further declined between 2015 and 2017. With the current average decline in notification rate and number of TB deaths however, the EU/EEA will not reach the targets by 2030.
